dedupe_keys.name: ditec wdn large scale dataset of hydraulic scenarios across water distribution networks

description: DiTEC-WDN is a large dataset of simulated hydraulic scenarios covering 36 water distribution networks, built by the DiTEC project at the University of Groningen for training and testing data-driven and graph machine learning models. Each network has 1,000 scenarios, each a time series of graphs whose nodes are reservoirs, junctions and tanks and whose edges are pipes, pumps and valves of specified types, with static parameters (pipe diameter, length and roughness, tank and pump properties) and time-varying demands and simulated hydraulic states. It is hosted on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0 (73 subsets, 1 to 10 billion rows), with the generation code on GitHub and Zenodo under MIT, and is described in Scientific Data (Truong et al., 2025). An earlier release covered 11 networks, including L-Town, C-Town and Anytown, as 7.2 GB of CSV files. Caveats: all states are simulated from benchmark models, not measured, parameter ranges were chosen by the authors, and the full dataset is very large. Simulation uses: surrogate hydraulic models, state estimation for digital twins and optimisation of network operation. Related records: EPANET (model-epanet) and BattLeDIM (data-battledim-leakage-detection-benchmark). The paper excludes leak, pipe-break and other anomalous scenarios; these are normal-operation synthetic benchmarks.
